{"record_id":"fun2026_planar_nemesis_fixed_exits","stage":"REVISION_AUDIT","arm":"plain","iteration":3,"parent_sha256":"02fc46d31ad86bc4334146bedfa47af48df7c78adeb4b4dabbbc2f5a4860fb14","complete":true,"claims":[{"idx":0,"claim":"Planar two-exit instances admit a cyclic two-gate decomposition. Let the exits be p,q and let B=N(p)∩N(q). Every component of G−({p,q}∪B) is adjacent to at most two vertices of B; when |B|≥3, those two are consecutive in the cyclic order of B around the exits.","claim_sha256":"13219d5d8d1ee914f2a86bf775924b0f1e304982df7bdc2d0c14542d5523ba1c","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"Let H be the K_{2,|B|} subgraph consisting only of the edges from p and q to B. For |B|≥3, H is simple, bipartite, and 2-connected, with |B|+2 vertices and 2|B| edges. Euler's formula gives |B| faces. Every facial boundary has length at least four, while the total facial-boundary length is 4|B|; hence every face is a 4-cycle p-b_i-q-b_{i+1}-p. Each component outside V(H), together with its incident attachment edges, is an H-bridge and its connected drawing lies in one face of H. Its B-attachments are therefore among that face's two consecutive gates. For |B|≤2, the bound is immediate. Extra edges of G do not invalidate the argument because H is used as a non-induced plane subgraph.","witness":"none","search_method":"Independent plane-embedding proof using Euler's formula and the face containment of bridges of a 2-connected plane subgraph.","checker_path":"none"},{"idx":1,"claim":"There is a linear-time classification when the exits have the same independent neighborhood. After deleting a possible irrelevant edge pq, suppose N(p)=N(q)=B and B is independent. The fugitive wins exactly when (i) s∈{p,q}∪B, (ii) s has a neighbor in B, or (iii) s has a neighbor w having two distinct neighbors in B.","claim_sha256":"14d050d86ce31db917e324859ecf354532783da6f04ad854c58a4381baa24393","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"Conditions (i) and (ii) give an immediate exit or a move to a gate whose two exit edges cannot both be deleted before the next move. Under (iii), after moving to w, the two three-edge configurations wb_i,b_ip,b_iq are edge-disjoint, so the first deletion leaves one intact; after moving to that gate, one of its two exit edges survives. Conversely, if all three conditions fail, after the first move the current outside component has at most two boundary gates and the current vertex sees at most one. Nemesis prepares that gate, or an arbitrary boundary gate if none is currently adjacent. The invariant is that at most one boundary gate remains fresh and it is not adjacent to the current outside vertex. Nemesis prepares it as soon as it becomes adjacent and kills the remaining exit edge immediately after a prepared gate is entered. Independence of B forces departure from a dead gate into a component having that dead gate plus at most one other boundary gate, preserving the invariant. Mandatory deletions make the play finite. The conditions are testable by linear adjacency scans. Exact minimax agreed with the formula on 19,747 starting positions across all 2,855 labelled instances through seven vertices satisfying the independent common-neighborhood and two-boundary-component properties.","witness":"none","search_method":"Proved both directions via explicit fugitive strategies and a prepare-then-kill Nemesis invariant; exhaustively checked all small labelled instances satisfying the structural premise with Boolean bitmask minimax.","checker_path":"/tmp/open_frontier_paired_v2/fun2026_planar_nemesis_fixed_exits/audit-revision/plain/iter_3/iter3_exact_audit_checker.py"},{"idx":2,"claim":"Two broader target-relevant subclasses are linearly solvable: (a) the graph induced by regular vertices is a forest, with arbitrary degrees; or (b) every regular vertex has degree at most three, with arbitrary exit degrees.","claim_sha256":"9914a3295a918cf5ee2366fcfd0c5e54547314d982b2995b6490e9f303eb5e43","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"After handling a start at an exit and discarding an exit-exit edge, replace each regular-exit edge vx by a distinct leaf-exit edge vx_v. This is a bijection on every edge relevant before escape. At every regular position and corresponding deleted-edge set, a path to an original exit exists iff a path to a fresh exit leaf exists: truncate an original path at its first exit for one direction and reverse the replacement for the other. Thus all regular moves, Nemesis deletions, trapping events, and strategies correspond. If the regular core is a forest, adding exit leaves leaves each relevant component a tree. If regular degrees are at most three, the transformation preserves those degrees and gives each new exit degree one, so the transformed graph has maximum degree three. The source-contained linear-time theorem therefore applies, and the transformation is linear-sized. Exhaustive minimax confirmed exit-splitting equivalence for all 1,098 simple labelled graphs through five vertices and all 3,208 regular starting positions.","witness":"none","search_method":"Established an edge-for-edge game-tree reduction, then exhaustively compared original and split-exit games on every small labelled simple graph.","checker_path":"/tmp/open_frontier_paired_v2/fun2026_planar_nemesis_fixed_exits/audit-revision/plain/iter_3/iter3_exact_audit_checker.py"},{"idx":3,"claim":"The binary-escape-tree condition is not necessary even for planar simple graphs with exactly two exits. A seven-vertex counterexample has exits p,q, start s, regular vertices a,b,c,z, and edges pa,pb,qa,qb,ab,az,bz,bc,cz,cs.","claim_sha256":"1d8ced434b96c1b7f8fe9208fed92e3bf61417e86df89a2e9836c9749ac9113f","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"A combinatorial rotation-system search found five facial orbits, so V−E+F=7−10+5=2 and certifies a spherical embedding. The proposed strategy is sound: play s-c. If bc is deleted, play c-z; the edge-disjoint triples za,ap,aq and zb,bp,bq ensure one intact route remains after the next deletion, and its two exit edges survive one further deletion. If bc is not deleted, play c-b. A surviving bp or bq wins immediately; if both were deleted, they were exactly the first two deletions, leaving ba,ap,aq intact, so b-a followed by a surviving exit edge wins. After splitting exit incidences, the only possible roots within distance one of s are s and c. Vertex s has only one incident edge. A full binary tree rooted at c cannot use regular leaf s, so its children must be b and z; with parent c, z would need both a and b as children, repeating b. Exhaustive enumeration of all 2^10 transformed edge subsets independently found no binary escape tree at either root.","witness":"Vertices {p,q,s,a,b,c,z}, exits {p,q}, and edges {pa,pb,qa,qb,ab,az,bz,bc,cz,cs}; winning strategy: s-c, then c-z if bc was deleted and otherwise c-b, with the subsequent choices described in the evidence.","search_method":"Exact Boolean minimax, exhaustive full-binary-tree edge-subset enumeration, and an exact combinatorial spherical rotation-system certificate.","checker_path":"/tmp/open_frontier_paired_v2/fun2026_planar_nemesis_fixed_exits/audit-revision/plain/iter_3/iter3_exact_audit_checker.py"},{"idx":4,"claim":"An exact recurrence gives PSPACE membership and an O*(8^n) planar algorithm, although not a polynomial classification. For deleted-edge set D and current regular vertex v, W(D,v) holds iff some surviving move vw reaches an exit or, for every surviving edge e Nemesis might delete, w remains connected to an exit and W(D∪{e},w) holds.","claim_sha256":"22b3f683058b078388aa871244e8a99b38408aea5f752384421a3ccdf271a53d","verdict":"VERIFIED","evidence":"With the existential move scoped over the complete bracket, the recurrence is W(D,v)=∃vw∈E−D [w is an exit or ∀e∈E−D (w remains exit-connected in G−(D∪{e}) and W(D∪{e},w))]. This exactly represents the fugitive move followed by every possible mandatory Nemesis deletion. Induction on the number of surviving edges proves correctness, including terminal disconnection and immediate escape. There are at most n·2^m states and polynomial work per state, giving O*(2^m) time with memoization. For a planar simple graph, m≤3n−6 for n≥3, hence O*(8^n). A depth-first evaluation has depth at most m and polynomial-sized masks and frames, proving PSPACE membership. On all 1,098 simple labelled graphs through five vertices and 5,404 starts, the recurrence agreed exactly with an independently implemented evaluator having separate fugitive and Nemesis phases.","witness":"none","search_method":"Induction on surviving edges, state-count and space analysis, plus exhaustive comparison against a separately phased exact game evaluator.","checker_path":"/tmp/open_frontier_paired_v2/fun2026_planar_nemesis_fixed_exits/audit-revision/plain/iter_3/iter3_exact_audit_checker.py"}],"confirmed_refutations":[],"target_verdict":"VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS","claimed_resolution_verdict":"ACCURATE","target_evidence":"The exact target asks for a classification of every planar simple graph with exactly two exits, either by a polynomial-time algorithm or by a matching hardness result. The draft explicitly states that it supplies neither. Its verified cyclic decomposition, linear algorithms for three restricted families, planar counterexample to necessity of the escape-tree condition, and exact exponential recurrence are material target-relevant advances but do not settle the unrestricted class. Therefore VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS is appropriate, the claimed PARTIAL resolution is ACCURATE, and the headline/final writeup does not overstate target coverage.","overall":"VERIFIED","checks_performed":["Read only the authorized source JSON and iteration-3 draft JSON; did not use the web, any retrieval database, treatment receipt, prior frontier run, verification report, or other solution.","Read the exact target and the source-contained formal move-then-delete rules and linear-time theorem before assessing coverage and reductions.","Confirmed the draft file SHA-256 is 02fc46d31ad86bc4334146bedfa47af48df7c78adeb4b4dabbbc2f5a4860fb14.","Independently proved the K_{2,|B|} facial decomposition and audited its small-|B|, extra-edge, and disconnected-ambient-graph cases.","Proved the same-independent-neighborhood classification using explicit winning strategies and a maintained fresh/prepared/dead gate invariant.","Proved exit-incidence splitting preserves every pre-escape game state and checked the resulting forest and maximum-degree-three cases.","Checked the seven-vertex witness by exact minimax, exhaustive binary-tree search, and a spherical rotation-system certificate.","Proved the recurrence by induction and independently compared it with an explicit two-phase game evaluator.","Ran /tmp/open_frontier_paired_v2/fun2026_planar_nemesis_fixed_exits/audit-revision/plain/iter_3/iter3_exact_audit_checker.py successfully using only integer bitmasks and Boolean/combinatorial decisions; checker SHA-256 is c0d31a22092c8752c6034b00c910a2d0af08cfea68f998e4a28164d312d7d084."]}--- END INDEPENDENT AUDIT ---
